ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

3. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

7. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

8. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

12. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Intonation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
